meta.title: Korean Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 517 expressions · 41 everyday, 316 idioms, 160 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 517 Korean set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 41 everyday phrases, 316 idioms and 160 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Korean → English and English → Korean — each with a schedule of its own. A companion to the stage decks and not one of them: nothing here is a headword of Stage A, B or C. — The PHRASES are everyday formulas from English Wiktionary's list (greetings, thanks, the words before and after a meal), picked by hand with its slang, dialect and profanity left out. The IDIOMS and PROVERBS are English Wiktionary's, then those of KRDict, the National Institute of the Korean Language's dictionary for learners, taking only an expression every word of which is taught in the stage decks, the commonest words first. A KRDict expression's meaning is KRDict's English definition, with its English rendering — often word for word — in italics beneath; those 382 carry no romanization, KRDict giving none for an expression. 44 of the 517 have example sentences. — Phrases, the Wiktionary idioms and proverbs, their meanings and romanization: English Wiktionary via kaikki.org (CC BY-SA 4.0). The other idioms and proverbs: KRDict (한국어기초사전, NIKL, CC BY-SA 2.0 KR). Example sentences: Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR) and Wiktionary.
